security_audit.summary: All 16 static findings are false positives caused by TypeScript template literals, Markdown fences, or defensive adversarial test data. However, the adversarial runner counts every processing exception as a pass, which can conceal crashes and inflate reported safety.

remediation.issue: The adversarial runner records agent processing exceptions as successful test outcomes.
remediation.suggestion: Record unexpected exceptions as failures, preserve timeout-specific handling, and report an explicit error status separately from detector results.

content.user_title: Evaluate LLM Agents with Reliable Test Suites
content.value_statement: Single-run checks hide stochastic failures and production regressions. This skill designs repeatable evaluations with behavioral, adversarial, statistical, and leakage tests.
actual_capabilities: Design repeated-run evaluations with pass rates, confidence intervals, latency metrics, and behavior consistency.
Define behavioral contracts for required, prohibited, and context-dependent agent actions.
Build adversarial suites for prompt injection, role confusion, boundary cases, output manipulation, and tool abuse.
Compare baseline and updated agents to identify statistically significant regressions.
Assess production readiness with real samples, adversarial variants, edge cases, and load metrics.
Detect benchmark leakage across training examples, system prompts, memorized completions, and RAG retrieval.
limitations: Provides illustrative TypeScript patterns, not a complete runnable framework.
Depends on project-specific Agent, TestCase, detector, and statistical helper implementations.
Does not cover model training metrics, fairness and bias testing, or user experience research.
The adversarial runner example treats processing errors as passes and requires correction before use.

use_cases.title: Build Agent Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Create repeated behavioral and regression tests that produce measurable release criteria.

use_cases.title: Assess Model Reliability
use_cases.description: Measure stochastic performance, confidence intervals, consistency, and benchmark leakage across agent versions.

use_cases.title: Monitor Production Agents
use_cases.description: Compare benchmarks with real traffic, edge cases, adversarial variants, and load behavior.

prompt_templates.scenario: Turning product rules into testable expectations

prompt_templates.title: Design Adversarial Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design adversarial tests for [agent and tools]. Cover prompt injection, role confusion, boundary conditions, output manipulation, and tool misuse.
prompt_templates.scenario: Testing safety and resilience before release

output_examples.input: Evaluate a customer support agent that processes refunds.
output_examples.output: Run 20 trials per case, enforce refund-policy contracts, test injection resistance, compare latency, and block deployment on critical violations.

output_examples.input: Investigate a release that passes benchmarks but fails in production.
output_examples.output: Compare anonymized production samples, adversarial variants, edge cases, and load latency against the benchmark baseline before adjusting the release gate.

output_examples.input: Check whether benchmark data leaked into an agent.
output_examples.output: Search for training matches, prompt overlap, memorized completions, and RAG retrieval of expected answers. Replace affected tests before reporting results.

best_practices: Run stochastic tests multiple times and report distributions instead of one result.
Use production-derived samples only after anonymization and access review.
Combine correctness, safety, reliability, efficiency, and human preference metrics.
anti_patterns: Do not treat agent errors or timeouts as successful adversarial outcomes.
Do not release an agent based only on aggregate benchmark scores.
Do not reuse evaluation examples in training data, prompts, or retrieval sources.

faq.question: Does this skill execute a complete evaluation framework?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript patterns and evaluation methods that require integration with your agent and test infrastructure.

faq.question: How many times should each stochastic test run?
faq.answer: The examples use at least 10 runs. Increase repetitions when failure costs are high or confidence intervals remain wide.

faq.question: Can it test prompt injection resistance?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes direct, encoded, role-confusion, boundary, output-manipulation, and tool-abuse cases with expected noncompliance.

faq.question: Does it support production monitoring?
faq.answer: It outlines baseline comparisons, real-sample checks, edge-case testing, load metrics, and regression alerts.

faq.question: Can it detect benchmark leakage?
faq.answer: It checks training similarity, system-prompt overlap, memorized completions, and RAG retrieval of expected answers.

faq.question: What must be fixed before using the adversarial runner example?
faq.answer: Change exception handling so unexpected errors fail tests or receive a separate error status. Do not count every exception as a pass.
